title: Dual-Camera High-Speed Carrier
description: The split between what BRIEF.md fixes and what it leaves open. Every fixed_requirements entry carries the verbatim brief text that substantiates it, bound to the recorded brief digest. An open_decisions entry is a choice for the design agent: record it in 'chosen' with 'rationale', and never move it into fixed_requirements. Missing details are design freedom, not permission to fabricate unstated user requirements.

brief.authority: supplied by the benchmark; authoritative; preserved byte for byte and never edited

derivation.method: BRIEF.md was read and split; no design decision was taken. Every fixed_requirements entry, and every spec-table row sourced from the brief, carries a quotation that was checked by literal substring match against the brief bytes digested above. The build refuses to emit this file if any quotation is not found.
derivation.review: two rounds of adversarial review against the brief, looking for invented requirements, lost requirements, evidence supporting a weaker claim than the one made beside it, and worksheet questions that presuppose their own answer

fixed_requirements.requirement: The board is a compact carrier — compactness is a stated property of the design, not an optional goal.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Design a compact carrier for two small digital camera modules

fixed_requirements.requirement: The carrier hosts two small digital camera modules.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Design a compact carrier for two small digital camera modules and a host processor/FPGA connection.

fixed_requirements.requirement: The carrier provides a connection to a host processor or FPGA.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: two small digital camera modules and a host processor/FPGA connection

fixed_requirements.requirement: The camera interface must be a realistic modern one. The brief offers MIPI CSI-2 and a serializer/deserializer architecture as examples ("such as"), so either satisfies it, but the list is not closed and another realistic modern camera interface is equally admissible.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Use a realistic modern camera interface such as MIPI CSI-2 or a serializer/deserializer architecture

fixed_requirements.requirement: Parts must be selected such that public layout guidance exists for them — a device with no public layout guidance is excluded by the brief's own selection criterion.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: serializer/deserializer architecture, selecting parts with public layout guidance

fixed_requirements.requirement: The board must include camera power rails.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Include camera power rails, clocks/control, ESD where exposed, and a host connector.

fixed_requirements.requirement: The board must include clocks and control signalling for the cameras.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Include camera power rails, clocks/control, ESD where exposed

fixed_requirements.requirement: ESD protection must be included where exposed. The brief states the obligation but not the exposure boundary, which is left open (OPEN-12).
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: clocks/control, ESD where exposed, and a host connector.

fixed_requirements.requirement: The board must include a host connector.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: ESD where exposed, and a host connector. Make the mechanical connector placement restrictive enough

fixed_requirements.requirement: Mechanical connector placement must be restrictive enough that high-speed lane escape and return paths are genuinely constrained — the design must not relieve this difficulty by spreading connectors out.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Make the mechanical connector placement restrictive enough that high-speed lane escape and return paths matter.

fixed_requirements.requirement: Where the brief is silent, the design agent must make and document reasonable engineering decisions rather than invent hidden user requirements.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: make and document reasonable engineering decisions rather than inventing hidden user requirements

fixed_requirements.requirement: Stated brief requirements are authoritative and must not be overridden by later design convenience.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Treat stated requirements as authoritative; where the brief leaves choices open

fixed_requirements.requirement: The repository stays a consumer of the shared PCBA_AutoDesignAndTest toolkit; board-specific logic must not be pushed into the toolkit.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: The repository should remain a consumer of the shared `PCBA_AutoDesignAndTest` toolkit rather than accumulating board-specific logic in the toolkit.

open_decisions.decision: Which realistic modern camera interface to adopt: direct MIPI CSI-2 from the cameras to the host, a serializer/deserializer architecture between them, or another realistic modern camera link — and, once chosen, whether it is applied uniformly to both cameras.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names MIPI CSI-2 and SerDes only as examples ('such as') of a 'realistic modern camera interface'; it neither chooses between them nor restricts the choice to those two.

open_decisions.decision: Which camera-interface silicon (serializer, deserializer, CSI bridge, aggregator or repeater, if any) to use, and how many of them.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief constrains only that the chosen parts have public layout guidance; it names no device, vendor or family.

open_decisions.decision: Which camera modules to target, their pinout, and how the two cameras are aggregated or presented to the host (independent links, shared link, or combined).
open_decisions.why_open: The brief says 'two small digital camera modules' and nothing about the module family, its interface width, or how the two streams reach the host.

open_decisions.decision: Lane count, data rate and per-link bandwidth budget for the camera and host links.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states no resolution, frame rate, pixel depth or bit rate; the entire bandwidth budget is unfixed.

open_decisions.decision: Camera-side and host-side connector selection: type, pitch, mating orientation, retention, and pin assignment.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires 'a host connector' and treats connectors as compact and restrictively placed, but names no connector type and gives no pinout.

open_decisions.decision: Board outline, overall dimensions, camera-to-camera spacing and baseline, mounting hole pattern, keepouts and any enclosure interface.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief says only that the carrier is 'compact'; it states no dimension, mounting scheme or mechanical envelope.

open_decisions.decision: The exact stackup: dielectric materials and thicknesses, copper weights, reference-plane assignment per signal layer, and the actual layer count.
open_decisions.why_open: Metadata gives 6 as a *likely* layer count, not a requirement, and neither the brief nor metadata specifies materials, thicknesses or plane assignment.

open_decisions.decision: Target differential and single-ended impedances, tolerance, and whether impedance is controlled by the fabricator.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states no impedance target; it only makes return paths matter. The number has to come from the interface and stackup eventually chosen, not from the brief.

open_decisions.decision: Intra-pair skew, inter-pair skew and total length-matching budgets, and how they are apportioned across the link.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief is silent on timing budgets; these follow from the interface and silicon eventually chosen.

open_decisions.decision: Power architecture: input rail(s) and where power enters, number of rails, rail voltages, regulator topology (switching, linear, or pass-through), sequencing, and current budget.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires 'camera power rails' but names no voltage, no current, no source and no regulator type.

open_decisions.decision: Power-filtering strategy: decoupling scheme, ferrite/pi filtering on camera analog and PLL supplies, plane splits, and how filtering is verified.
open_decisions.why_open: 'Power filtering' is a benchmark stressor, not a specified solution; the brief prescribes no filter topology or component values.

open_decisions.decision: Which nets count as 'exposed' for ESD purposes, and what protection strategy is applied to each (device type, placement, and the capacitance budget it must respect on high-speed lanes).
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires 'ESD where exposed' without defining the exposure boundary, the stress level, or any protection component.

open_decisions.decision: Clock architecture: whether cameras are clocked from an on-board source, from the host, or recovered from the link; and the jitter budget for that source.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires 'clocks/control' but does not say where clocks originate or what jitter performance is needed.

open_decisions.decision: Camera control plane: which control bus is used, addressing/muxing for two cameras, and reset/power-down/strobe/sync signalling.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief groups control with clocks in one phrase and specifies no bus, no address scheme and no sideband signals.

open_decisions.decision: Where exactly the restrictive connector placement is applied — which edge or face each connector sits on, and which routing hardship that placement is chosen to create.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief mandates that placement be restrictive enough to make lane escape and return paths matter, but leaves the specific geometry that produces this to the design agent.

open_decisions.decision: Via strategy for lane escape: via type (through, blind/buried, microvia), stitching-via placement around escapes and layer transitions, the fabrication class this implies, and the cost/capability policy used to weigh it.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief is silent on fabrication class and on cost; this follows from the chosen connector pitch and stackup and from the agent's own justification policy.

open_decisions.decision: Multi-camera synchronisation: whether the two cameras must be frame-synchronised, and if so by what mechanism.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states two cameras on one carrier but says nothing about synchronisation between them.

open_decisions.decision: Test, bring-up and manufacturing-test provisions: test points, probe access on high-speed lanes, programming/debug access, fiducials, and the bring-up sequence itself.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief does not mention test or bring-up access at all, and prescribes no order in which the board is brought up.

open_decisions.decision: Fabricator and assembly process targets, and the resulting minimum trace/space, annular ring and component-placement rules.
open_decisions.why_open: Neither the brief nor the metadata names a fabricator or process class.

open_decisions.decision: Thermal handling for the interface silicon and regulators, including copper area, via arrays and any airflow assumption.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states no thermal, ambient or power-dissipation requirement; compactness raises the question but does not answer it.

open_decisions.decision: What kind of published source counts as 'public layout guidance' for the chosen parts (device-vendor layout or application note, standards-body document, fabricator design rules, published reference design), and how far the layout rules actually used are traced and cited back to it.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief conditions part selection on public layout guidance existing but qualifies the guidance in no way and never states that the rules used must be traceable to it; both the admissible source class and the citation discipline are the agent's call.
